items.title: My tenant got arrested for violation of probation and has left me with a lot of questions (California)
items.text:
My tenant got arrested for violation of probation and has left me with a lot of questions (California)
Technically, it's my girlfriends tenant because she owns the house but we live together. So, one of our tenants is currently on probation for apparently stabbing his stepfather. His probation officer came by the house while my girlfriend I were gone and in plain view in our bedroom was my pistol. According to terms of his probation, he is not allowed to live in a home where there are firearms, so he was arrested. The probation officer took the gun with him, but left us no contact information or any instructions on how to get our weapon back. Second, since our tenant obviously can't live with us anymore, what do we do with his stuff? I don't believe that he has any family up here that he talks to, and he's got a lot of really nice stuff that I don't want to get damaged. When he originally rented from my girlfriend, he rented the master bedroom. now that my girlfriend and I moved back in, we had a verbal agreement that once the other tenant in the house moved out he would take over his room and my girlfriend I would take over the master bedroom. Would it be illegal for us to move his property into the separate bedroom and us take over the master bedroom? Finally, he has a snake. I don't like snakes. I don't know anything about caring for snakes. I am very concerned that the snake may die because of my ignorance about reptiles. Do I have to get permission from him to place the snake in a foster home so that it can be properly care for?

Follow-up question. What if he is in jail beyond the time of the eviction? If we give him a 60 days notice of eviction, and he gets a year or two in jail do we still have to wait the 60 days to get his stuff out? Or can we move his property out since technically he has a new residence?

I worked for a private ambulance company. I was on hour 12 of what was supposed to be an 8 hour shift. I was going back to the ambulance, and I tossed my tablet onto the passenger seat so I could go to the back and help my partner set up the cot. Somehow, the tablet bounced off the seat and landed between the seat and the door, just as the door was closing and it shattered the screen. That was our last call of the night, so we went back to the station, I advised dispatch is what had happened and wrote an incident report. The next day, the owner of the company has the dispatch supervisor call me and tell me that I'm fired because they have had too many people destroying the tablets. I ended up having one of my friends that still work there apologize to the dispatcher, because I should not have taken my anger out on him. That company had a lot of issues and I think it's best that I was let go. I think the fact that I upgraded calls to ALS when it was needed did not help me either. I mean, if we don't transport we don't get paid. But when you have a 45 year old man who is at a care facility because of a stroke who has an unattended fall where he strikes his head and draws blood and then begins complaining of headache and vision loss, I'd like to think you worry less about money and more about patient care. The company worried more about money
